answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. What makes it robust is that honest graders are financially motivated to reject the cluster, so fake votes lose their value before verdicts are tallied. Consider a falcon as the anchor of the cost.
